description: API usage through an EdgeGuard (eggrd) edge: per-route rate, errors and latency, per-upstream health, the time the edge itself adds, connections against the cap, refused client certificates, PROXY protocol headers, upstream pools and their ejections, and the top consumers. Reference template; see the monitoring/ directory in the repo.

panels.description: 99th percentile of the time the edge itself adds to a proxied request: its time to response headers less the time spent waiting on the upstream (edgeguard_edge_overhead_seconds).
panels.title: Edge overhead p99

panels.description: Share of requests forwarded to any upstream that failed or were answered 5xx (edgeguard_upstream_requests_total, result != ok).
panels.title: Upstream error ratio

panels.description: The fullest listener's open connections as a share of server.max_connections. No data when no listener has a cap.
panels.title: Connections vs cap

panels.description: TLS handshakes refused for their client certificate, per second: none presented, an unknown CA, revoked or expired. These never reach the access log.
panels.title: Client certificates refused

panels.description: Requests per second by route: the configured name or prefix of the matching [[upstreams]] or [[ratelimit.routes]] entry, default for the rest.
panels.title: Requests by route

panels.description: Share of each route's requests answered 5xx, by the edge or the upstream.
panels.title: 5xx ratio by route

panels.description: 99th percentile time to response headers, by route.
panels.title: p99 latency by route

panels.description: Share of each upstream's requests that failed or were answered 5xx. The alert EdgeGuardUpstreamErrorRatio fires above 5% for 5m.
panels.title: Error ratio by upstream

panels.description: How each upstream fails: connect_error (down or unreachable), tls_error (CA or client certificate), timeout, reset (closed mid-response), http_5xx, error.
panels.title: Failures by upstream and result

panels.description: 99th percentile time from sending a request to the upstream's response headers, for exchanges that got them (edgeguard_upstream_duration_seconds).
panels.title: Upstream p99 time to headers

panels.description: Time the edge adds to a proxied request the upstream answered, beyond waiting on it. Includes authentication, rate limiting, WAF and DLP.
panels.title: Edge overhead

panels.description: Open connections by listener, and server.max_connections where it is set.
panels.title: Connections and cap

panels.description: Failed TLS handshakes by listener and reason: client_cert (refused for its certificate), timeout, other. Connections that close before a ClientHello (load balancer TCP and PROXY protocol health checks) are not failures and are not shown here: they are edgeguard_tls_no_client_hello_total (eggrd 0.7.0-rc.2 and later; earlier versions counted them as other).
panels.title: TLS handshakes refused

panels.description: The ten consumers with the most requests over the dashboard's time range. A consumer is the authenticated principal (apikey:<id>, never the key; the Basic user; the JWT sub; the client certificate's name); _anon has none, _over_cap is past metrics.consumer_series_max.
panels.title: Top consumers by requests

panels.description: The ten consumers that moved the most bytes, request and response, headers included, over the dashboard's time range.
panels.title: Top consumers by bytes

panels.description: Requests per second answered 4xx or 5xx, for the ten consumers getting the most: a broken integration, an expired key, or a client over its limit.
panels.title: Consumers getting errors

panels.description: Requests carrying [trusted_client_cert_header], by what became of the certificate: accepted, untrusted_peer (dropped: not from trusted_proxies or trusted_proxy_names), invalid (not in the configured format), unverified (refused by its ca_path). Empty unless the header is on.
panels.title: Forwarded client certificates

panels.description: Connections on listeners with server.proxy_protocol, by what their header said: proxied (it named the client), local (the balancer's health check), missing (the trusted balancer sent none), direct (another peer, no header), and closed: untrusted (a header from outside proxy_protocol_trusted), invalid, timeout. Empty unless it is on.
panels.title: PROXY protocol headers

panels.description: For each [[upstreams]] pool target: 1 while it takes requests, 0 while it is out (failing its health check, or ejected after requests failed to connect to it). Requests go to the targets in rotation by the pool's balance, and to backup targets only when no other will. Empty without pools.
panels.title: Pool targets in rotation

panels.description: Active health checks of pool targets that failed: no answer within the timeout, or an answer outside 2xx/3xx. A target leaves rotation after health_check.unhealthy_after in a row.
panels.title: Failed health checks

panels.description: Pool targets taken out of rotation by requests, by reason: connect_error (eject_after failed connections in a row) or http_5xx (eject_after_5xx 5xx answers in a row). Each lasts eject_for; a target ejected again and again is flapping.
panels.title: Ejections
